must_fix: (criterion 1/4, highest impact) Extend mechanical pre-checks to catch multi-period column/entity mislabelling, not just citation format and arithmetic sums. TJX's dossier stated Q2 FY2027 net income as $1,243m; the actual figure is $1,520m -- $1,243m is the prior-year Q2 FY2026 column from the same press-release table. I independently WebFetched the same 8-K Ex-99.1 (accession 0000109198-26-000045) and confirmed both figures exactly match DA14's finding and the dossier's correction. Neither lead_dossier_precheck.py nor lead_xbrl_crosstie.py flagged this (both show empty flags for TJX). This is the fourth consecutive loop (Loop 5 GM/RJF entity conflation; Loop 6 COR guidance-checkpoint mislabel; Loop 7 PPG debt-component sum; Loop 8 this) where a load-bearing numeric error reaches a dossier and is caught only by the adversarial DA pass. Fix: add a self-check that records BOTH column values and dates for any figure cited from a two-column (current-vs-prior-period) source table, so a swap is caught before publication rather than after a new single-purpose check is retrofitted each loop.

(carried, confirmed by design, sixth consecutive loop) The verification gate correctly reads OPEN for exactly one reason: outputs/c1_consistency.json still names the pre-wave-5 build's content_sha256 while the live frozen build is 174b2544.... I ran code/lead_verify_gate.py myself and confirmed no holding is missing an independent DA-series fact-check and no FAIL is left uncorrected. This exact gap has been the sole open item in every loop from 3 through 8; recommend completing one full cycle (fix -> re-run C1 last -> gate reads PASS) before the next release so the mechanism is demonstrated to close in practice.

(minor, criterion 6) Add one explicit sentence to FINAL_REPORT section 6 prose (not just the ranking-tab JSON) stating that Financials currently binds two caps simultaneously (25% sector-weight cap and rule (l)'s 5-names-per-sector count cap): a sixth otherwise-eligible Financials name (MSCI) is excluded by the count rule alone, before the weight cap would even bind. The data already supports this (lead_j_sensitivity.json bench_near_misses); this is a wording fix, not new analysis.
